whatIs: Headless UI is a library of unstyled interactive components, such as menus, dialogs, tabs, listboxes or switches, that handles accessibility and keyboard handling and leaves the look in your hands. It has a React and a Vue version, and it's designed to be combined with Tailwind CSS.
It's a good fit when you want your interface to have its own design but don't want to rewrite the logic of an accessible combobox or modal.
uses: Building a user dropdown menu that can be navigated with the keyboard and a screen reader.
Creating a searchable select (combobox) to pick a country or a tag in a form.
Showing a confirmation dialog with focus trapping that closes with Escape.
caveats: It comes with no styles: you have to dress each component with your own classes.
It only covers React and Vue, and the Vue version is still on the 1.x branch, with fewer components than the React one.
The catalog is limited (16 components), so pieces like tables or calendars you build yourself.
pricingNote: Open source under the MIT license.
idealFor: Teams with their own design that need accessible components already solved.
